text:
Eeli Tolvanen is in his first season with the Rangers after his years in Seattle, playing about 12 minutes a night in a depth role, with four goals and six points in 21 games. He hits (36) and blocks shots (19), which is the job.

The underlying numbers are weaker than the team's. The Rangers take 48% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than 6 points worse than without him, and 47% of the shot attempts. The goal results have been kind: New York has scored 5.3 more goals than expected during his shifts. His own finishing is fair, 4 goals on 3.6 expected.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season adds context: around replacement level and in the bottom 4% of forwards for creating offense, but also stuck with the weakest teammates in the league by their measure, which made his raw numbers look worse than his own effect. Our model compares him to Erik Haula and Jordan Martinook. He has one goal since October. Our talent range has him around 13 for the year. He's a depth piece on a team whose depth has been winning its minutes, and that's the bar.
